title: Spike: Oracle PRD for next-stage portable+metal architecture hardening
description:
• It’s good, and it’s now a credible canonical pattern, but I wouldn’t call it “best possible” yet.

  What’s strong now:

  - portable + metal contract split is the right abstraction.
  - Snapshot + semantic-diff harness is strong enough to evolve safely.
  - Metal specialization lanes (typed helpers) are real and measurable.

  What I’d still do differently / next:

  1. Split GoCompiler.hx into smaller lowering modules (it’s still a god-file risk).
  2. Add a dedicated post-lowering readability pass for metal (to push generated Go closer to handwritten style).
  3. Finish selective hxrt inference/reporting as default in metal lanes.
  4. Formalize “orthogonal axes” config (strictness, runtime policy, interop policy) under profile presets.
  5. Add stronger metal-focused example(s) where the output is intentionally audited for idiomatic Go shape.
  6. Keep portable semantics as non-negotiable baseline and gate all metal optimizations against it.

  So: strong architecture direction, not end-state. I’d keep this direction and harden those six areas.
